syntax-highlight.context: Three lines of code made of solid blocks and plain dashes, the way coloured tokens look in an editor. Used for code theme settings, colouring toggles and developer tools.

format-document.context: Ragged lines on the left, an arrow, and neatly aligned lines on the right. Used for auto-format, tidy-up and prettify commands in code editors and document tools.

bracket-pair.context: A matching pair of curly braces with a small dot under each. Used for bracket matching, bracket colourisation and code block settings in editors.

split-editor.context: A window cut into two panes by a vertical line, each pane holding short lines of code. Used for split view in code editors and side by side file comparison.

text-direction-vertical.context: A column of small letter blocks beside a downward arrow. Used for vertical writing mode, top to bottom text flow and tategaki-style layouts.

view-thumbnails.context: A two by two grid of picture frames, each showing a tiny mountain. Used to switch a file or photo browser to thumbnail view.

miller-columns.context: Three narrow columns side by side with a highlighted row stepping down in each, as in a column file browser. Used for column view and drill-down navigation.

two-page-spread.context: An open book with two facing pages and a line of text on each. Used for two-page view in readers, PDF viewers and layout tools.

continuous-scroll-view.context: Two page rectangles stacked vertically with a double-headed arrow beside them. Used for continuous scroll mode in PDF and document viewers.

presentation-mode.context: A screen on a tripod stand showing a play triangle. Used for starting a slideshow or entering full-screen presenting.

slide-sorter.context: Six slide thumbnails in two columns with one of them outlined as selected. Used for slide sorter and slide overview views in presentation software.

speaker-notes.context: A slide above lines of notes with a small speech bubble. Used to open or edit presenter notes beneath a slide.

density-compact.context: Five horizontal lines packed tightly together. Used in tables and lists to switch to compact row spacing.

density-comfortable.context: Three horizontal lines spaced widely apart. Used in tables and lists to switch to comfortable, roomy row spacing.

ar-view.context: A small cube framed by four corner brackets, like an augmented reality viewfinder. Used for viewing a 3D model in your own space.

view-3d.context: A wireframe cube with three short axis arrows rising from a corner. Used for 3D view modes, orientation gizmos and model viewers.

timeline-view.context: A horizontal line with three bars of different lengths staggered above and below it. Used for timeline and schedule views in planners and project tools.

focus-view.context: A single card in the centre with the edges of two more cards cut off at the left and right. Used for focus mode, carousels and cover-flow style browsing.

outline-mode.context: A circle and a square overlapping, both drawn as thin outlines with no fill. Used for wireframe or outline view in vector and design tools.

infinite-canvas.context: A fading grid of dots around an infinity sign. Used for endless whiteboards and pan-and-zoom workspaces.

card-flip.context: A card turned part way round with a curved arrow circling it. Used for flipping flashcards, turning a card over and showing its other side.

preview-pane.context: A window with a short list on the left and a page with an eye on the right. Used to toggle a preview or reading pane beside a file list.

hot-corner.context: A screen with a bright quarter circle in its top right corner and a pointer arrow heading into it. Used for hot corner and active screen corner settings.

screen-saver.context: A monitor whose screen shows a few small stars and a bouncing ball with its trail. Used for screen saver and idle display settings.

detach-tab.context: Two tabs on a bar with a third tab lifted off below and trailing short motion lines. Used for moving a tab into its own window.

tab-overview.context: A browser frame holding a two by two grid of tab thumbnails. Used for tab switcher and all-tabs overview screens.

vote-counter.context: An upward caret, a short number dash and a downward caret stacked in a column. Used for upvote and downvote controls with a score.

message-composer.context: A wide rounded text field with a paperclip at the left and a paper plane send button at the right. Used for chat and message input bars.

figure-caption.context: A picture frame with a mountain inside and a short caption line under it. Used for image captions and figure labels in documents.

callout-block.context: A rounded block with a thick bar down its left side, a small dot and two lines of text. Used for note, info and tip blocks inside documents.

labeled-divider.context: A horizontal line broken in the middle by a small rounded label. Used for dividers with text such as an or separator in forms and feeds.

user-chip.context: A rounded pill with a small avatar disc at the left end and a short name line. Used for user tags, assignee chips and mentions.

transfer-list.context: Two tall list panels side by side with a right arrow and a left arrow between them. Used for dual list boxes where items move between available and selected lists.

segmented-progress-bar.context: A row of four short separate bars, the first two tall and solid and the last two slim and empty. Used for step progress and multi-stage completion.

circular-slider.context: A round track with the arc filled two thirds of the way round and ending in a round knob. Used for dials, radial sliders and circular progress controls.

on-screen-joystick.context: A large ring with a smaller solid disc pushed toward its upper right. Used for virtual joysticks and touch thumbsticks in mobile games.

image-hotspot.context: A photo frame with a mountain and a small dot inside a pulsing ring above it. Used for clickable points on images and product tags.

annotation-pin.context: A speech bubble with a pointed tail like a map pin and a short dash inside it. Used for pinned comments on designs, maps and documents.

resizable-panels.context: A window split in two by a divider with a small grip handle in its middle. Used for draggable split panes and adjustable layouts.

floating-label-field.context: A text field whose short label sits in a gap in the top border with the entry text below it. Used for outlined inputs with floating labels.

input-prefix.context: A text field with a small separate box at its left end that holds a symbol. Used for inputs with a fixed prefix such as an at sign or currency mark.

input-with-button.context: A long text field joined at its right end to a solid rounded button. Used for subscribe, search and coupon fields with a submit button.

disclosure-row.context: A wide list row with a short label at the left and a small chevron at the right end. Used for settings rows and navigation list items that open another screen.

radio-card.context: A rounded card with a solid radio dot in its top left corner and two lines of text. Used for selectable option cards such as plan or shipping pickers.

pattern-fill.context: A square outline filled with evenly spaced diagonal hatching lines. Used for hatch and pattern fills in drawing and design tools.

noise-texture.context: A square outline scattered with tiny dots of different sizes. Used for grain, noise and speckle texture effects.

outline-stroke.context: A thick line turned into a hollow outline, shown above a thin solid line with an arrow between them. Used for the expand or outline stroke command in vector tools.

offset-path.context: A small solid star surrounded by a larger star outline at an even distance. Used for the offset path command that grows or shrinks a shape.

constrain-proportions.context: The letters W and H stacked with a bracket joining them on the right. Used for locking width and height ratio when resizing.

adjustment-layer.context: A diamond layer with a half filled circle on it, stacked above a second layer. Used for non-destructive adjustment layers in image editors.

component-variants.context: A dashed rounded frame holding a row of three small diamonds. Used for component variant sets in design systems.

stack-layout.context: Three equal blocks stacked in a column with even gaps and an arrow running down the side. Used for vertical stack and auto-layout direction settings.

flex-wrap.context: Two rows of small boxes with a bent arrow carrying the end of the top row around to the start of the next row. Used for wrapping layouts and flexbox wrap settings.

absolute-position.context: A frame with a small box pinned inside it and a dot on two sides marking its distance to the edges. Used for absolute and fixed position settings.

overflow-clip.context: A frame with a larger circle running through its right edge, the outside part drawn as dashes. Used for clip content and overflow hidden settings.

scroll-container.context: A box with lines of content running off its bottom and a slim scrollbar down its right side. Used for scrollable regions and overflow scroll settings.

background-removal.context: A head and shoulders silhouette in front of a checkerboard backdrop. Used for remove-background and transparent cutout tools in photo editors.

object-selection.context: A person silhouette inside a dashed outline with a pointer arrow at its lower right corner. Used for select subject and smart object selection tools.

rgb-channels.context: Three overlapping circles arranged in a triangle with a solid mark where all three meet. Used for red, green and blue colour channel controls.

cmyk-channels.context: Four overlapping rings arranged in a square, each with a solid dot of a different size. Used for CMYK print colour channels and separations.

key-meta.context: A rounded keycap with a small solid diamond in its centre. Used for the meta, command or super modifier key in shortcut lists.

cursor-rotate.context: An arrow pointer with a curved arrow sweeping around its tip. Used for rotate handles and rotation pointer states in editors.

ring-silent-switch.context: The edge of a phone with a small sliding switch sticking out and a bell on its face. Used for the ring and silent switch or mute toggle.

always-on-display.context: A phone with a dim clock ring and a single small notification dot on its dark screen. Used for always-on display and ambient lock screen settings.

locate-device.context: A phone with a radar arc on each side and a small dot above it. Used for find my device, ping and device tracking features.

device-transfer.context: Two phones side by side with a curved arrow arching from the left one to the right one. Used for moving data or files to a new device.

navigation-stack.context: Three screen cards stacked in depth with a back chevron on the front one. Used for screen history, push navigation and back stacks in apps.

page-curl.context: A page with its bottom right corner peeled up and folded back. Used for page turn animations, folded corners and dog-ear markers.

search-overlay.context: A dimmed screen with diagonal hatching below a bright search field across its top. Used for spotlight-style search and command palette overlays.

layout-three-pane.context: A window split into a narrow folder column, a middle list column and a wide reading pane. Used for three column mail and master-detail layouts.

layout-auth-split.context: A screen split in half with an image block on one side and two fields and a button on the other. Used for login and sign-up page templates.

layout-article.context: A page with a bold title bar, a wide picture block beneath it and a line of text. Used for article and blog post page templates.

layout-product-detail.context: A page with a square picture on the left and a title line, price dash and button on the right. Used for product page templates in shops.

isolation-mode.context: One bold circle standing out beside faint dashed outlines of a square and a small circle. Used for isolate and solo modes that hide everything but one object.

checkbox-tree.context: A parent checkbox with a branch line to two child checkboxes, the upper one ticked solid. Used for nested selection lists and permission trees.
